newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rights body elects new chairman.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rights body elects new chairman.

text.p: An adviser to President Suharto was elected chairman of Indonesia's National Commission on Human Rights on Tuesday, commission members said.

Munawir Sjadzali, a former foreign ministry official and minister of religion, was elected chairman by a 12-7 vote by the 21-member commission, defeating ruling Golkar party legislator Arnold Baramuli, commissioners said. Two people abstained.
Sjadzali, 71, is currently on the Supreme Advisory Council to Suharto.
"It is good for the institution," said commission deputy chairman Marzuki Darusman. "He (Sjadzali) is independent, he has integrity and he has vision."
The chairmanship has been vacant since the death in June of the commission's founding head, former Supreme Court justice Ali Said.
The commission has been criticised by Indonesia's powerful military for a preliminary report on riots that rocked Jakarta on July 27, the worst violence the city had seen in 20 years.
The commission report said five people had died, 149 were injured and 74 people had been reported missing.
The human rights body, founded in 1993, came under pressure from the government and the military to justify the findings. The military said only four people died and had not acknowledged any missing.

Darusman said the commission would be discussing its final report on the riots later this week. Darusman had been tipped for the commission chairmanship but said he did not put forward his name. He gave no reason.
